Inyoung · Listen & Shadow 02

Explaining the Paper
D O   E N G L I S H   W I T H   B R I A N
PART 1 · THE BACKGROUND
👤 Brian
Why ask this question at all?
애초에 왜 이 질문을 했어요?
at all — 애초에
💬 Inyoung
Normally, female mice that have never had pups either ignore pups or look after them.
보통 출산 경험이 없는 암컷 쥐는 새끼를 무시하거나 돌봐요.
pup — 새끼 · look after — 돌보다
같은 패턴으로 — Normally, the cells either divide or rest. · Usually, the animals either explore or hide.
💬 Inyoung
But animals feel many things at once — hunger, stress, hormones.
하지만 동물은 여러 가지를 동시에 느껴요 — 배고픔, 스트레스, 호르몬.
at once — 동시에
같은 패턴으로 — But neurons get many signals at once. · But patients deal with many problems at once.
💬 Inyoung
So the big question here is how the brain combines two states to change a social decision.
그래서 핵심 질문은 뇌가 두 상태를 어떻게 합쳐서 사회적 결정을 바꾸느냐예요.
combine — 합치다 · state — 상태
같은 패턴으로 — So the big question here is how the cell senses stress. · So the question is how two signals interact.
PART 2 · FIGURE 1
👤 Brian
How did they prove hunger causes the attack?
배고픔이 원인이라는 걸 어떻게 증명했어요?
prove — 증명하다 · cause — 일으키다
💬 Inyoung
The question here is whether hunger itself causes pup attack.
여기서 질문은 배고픔 자체가 새끼 공격을 일으키느냐예요.
whether — ~인지 아닌지
같은 패턴으로 — The question here is whether the drug works in vivo. · The question is whether this effect lasts.
💬 Inyoung
To test this, they took the food away for six hours.
이를 확인하려고 여섯 시간 동안 먹이를 치웠어요.
take away — 치우다
같은 패턴으로 — To test this, they removed the gene. · To test this, they blocked the channel.
💬 Inyoung
They also switched the hunger neurons on and off with a drug.
그리고 배고픔 뉴런을 약물로 켜고 껐어요.
switch on and off — 켜고 끄다
같은 패턴으로 — They switched the pathway on with light. · They turned the gene off in adult mice.
💬 Inyoung
What they found was that about sixty percent of the hungry mice attacked.
발견한 건, 굶은 쥐의 약 60%가 새끼를 공격했다는 거예요.
what they found was that — 발견한 건 ~였다
같은 패턴으로 — What they found was that the effect was reversible. · What we found was that the cells survived.
💬 Inyoung
This tells us the switch runs from the hunger neurons into the parenting area.
이건 배고픔 뉴런에서 육아 영역으로 가는 경로가 스위치라는 걸 말해줘요.
switch — 스위치 · run from A into B — A에서 B로 이어지다
같은 패턴으로 — This tells us the effect depends on sex. · This tells us the signal starts in the gut.
PART 3 · FIGURE 2
👤 Brian
If hunger causes it, why did only sixty percent attack?
배고픈데 왜 60%만 공격했어요?
only — ~만
💬 Inyoung
They were equally hungry. The difference was the oestrous cycle.
배고픔 정도는 같았어요. 차이는 발정 주기였어요.
equally — 똑같이 · oestrous cycle — 발정 주기
같은 패턴으로 — They were equally active. The difference was age. · The groups were the same size. The difference was diet.
💬 Inyoung
What mattered was the balance between the two hormones, not the amount of each.
각 호르몬의 양이 아니라 둘 사이의 균형이 중요했어요.
balance — 균형 · matter — 중요하다
같은 패턴으로 — What mattered was the timing, not the dose. · What mattered was the ratio, not the total.
💬 Inyoung
This tells us hormones set the odds, and hunger pulls the trigger.
이건 호르몬이 확률을 정하고, 배고픔이 방아쇠를 당긴다는 걸 말해줘요.
set the odds — 확률을 정하다 · pull the trigger — 방아쇠를 당기다
같은 패턴으로 — Genes set the odds, and the environment pulls the trigger. · Stress sets the stage, and sleep loss pulls the trigger.
PART 4 · FIGURE 3
👤 Brian
Where do the two signals actually meet?
두 신호는 어디서 만나요?
signal — 신호 · meet — 만나다
💬 Inyoung
They listened to one neuron at a time with patch-clamp recording.
한 뉴런씩 전기 활동을 들어봤어요.
patch-clamp recording — 단일 뉴런 전기 기록 · at a time — 한 번에
같은 패턴으로 — They imaged one cell at a time. · We tested one sample at a time.
💬 Inyoung
In the attackers, the neurons were quiet and harder to switch on.
공격한 쥐의 뉴런은 조용했고, 잘 켜지지 않았어요.
quiet — 조용한 · switch on — 켜다
같은 패턴으로 — In the treated group, the cells were smaller. · In older mice, the neurons were slower.
💬 Inyoung
That's because the channels that keep the neurons ready to fire were turned down.
그 이유는 뉴런을 준비 상태로 유지하는 채널이 꺼졌기 때문이에요.
fire — 발화하다 · turn down — 약하게 하다
같은 패턴으로 — That's because the receptor was blocked. · That's because the signal was turned down.
💬 Inyoung
Hormones set how many channels there are, and hunger decides how many are shut.
호르몬은 채널의 개수를, 배고픔은 채널을 끄는 정도를 정해요.
decide — 정하다 · shut — 닫힌
같은 패턴으로 — Genes set how many receptors there are. · Diet decides how much is stored.
PART 5 · FIGURE 4
👤 Brian
Does it hold in a living, behaving mouse?
살아 있는 뇌에서도 그런가요?
hold — (사실로) 유지되다 · behaving — 행동하는
💬 Inyoung
They put a tiny microscope on the head and tracked the same neurons.
머리에 작은 현미경을 달아서 같은 뉴런을 추적했어요.
track — 추적하다
같은 패턴으로 — They put a sensor on the wrist and tracked sleep. · We tracked the same cells for a week.
💬 Inyoung
When the attack started, the neurons moved into one lasting state.
공격이 시작되면 뉴런들이 하나의 지속적인 상태로 들어갔어요.
lasting — 지속적인
같은 패턴으로 — When the drug kicked in, the cells moved into a new state. · When the task began, activity shifted.
💬 Inyoung
This tells us aggression is a brain state, and it's more than a reflex.
이건 공격이 반사가 아니라 뇌의 상태라는 걸 말해줘요.
reflex — 반사 · aggression — 공격성
같은 패턴으로 — This tells us memory is a process, and it's more than storage. · This tells us the response is learned.
